subject: SLO acceptance testing checklist & reporting playbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@nebulahealth.com>, ops+prod@nebulahealth.com <ops+prod@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SLO acceptance testing checklist & reporting playbook

Aaron / Ops team — thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a lightweight draft that captures what we discussed for performance acceptance and ongoing SLA reporting. I wanted to summarize the immediate next steps and the acceptance-testing checklist so we can lock a canary window.

High-level summary (requested during call):
- Latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 400ms for inference API (single-turn text generation). Streaming tail target: 99th percentile time-to-first-bytes <= 200ms for streaming-enabled routes.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline burst capacity for your reserved pool targeting 300 concurrent requests, sustained throughput goal ~4k tokens/sec across the fleet.
- Measurement method: server-side timing (Redwood ingress to final chunk emitted). See measurement section in the attached PDF.
- Exclusions: customer network issues, scheduled maintenance windows, attempts that fail client-side validation. Also proposed a 30s cold-start exclusion for the first request after model container spin-up (we discussed this live).
- Reporting cadence: daily aggregated metrics (csv + dashboard), weekly incident digests, monthly SLA summary PDF.
- Remedies: tiered credits for monthly SLA misses (outlined in "slo-measurement-draft.pdf"), plus predefined rollback policy for canary failures.

Acceptance-testing checklist (short):
1) Confirm test API keys and endpoints — Redwood to provide test keys with identical routing/profile.
2) Define canary traffic profile (70% short requests < 128 tokens, 30% long tail up to 2k tokens).
3) Pick three test days (2–4 hour windows) where we run controlled load + synthetic streaming sessions.
4) Redwood will deliver raw per-request logs and aggregated CSV for the window within 24 hours.
5) Agree on measurement artifacts (p50/p95/p99, mean throughput, concurrency histogram).

Next steps / asks from Nebula:
- Please confirm a procurement contact (procurement@nebulahealth.com is ok?) and SOC2 evidence recipient (we can share an artifact link).
- Can you approve tentative canary window Oct 5–7, 0800–1200 PT? If not, propose alternatives.

I've attached: slo-measurement-draft.pdf (measurement definitions & exclusions) and call-recording-20260929.mp3. Will follow up with the reporting-playbook spreadsheet after we confirm scope.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128

From: Aaron Li <aaron.li@nebulahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+prod@nebulahealth.com <ops+prod@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO acceptance testing checklist & reporting playbook

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Streaming semantics: for our use case the streaming path is critical. We need the reporting to include both time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and per-chunk inter-arrival distribution (we saw variability in previous vendors). Can Redwood extract chunk timestamps in the artifact?
2) Cold-start handling: the 30s exclusion sounds reasonable; can we instead define it as "first request to a model instance within 60s of no traffic"? We have some unpredictable traffic during clinical hours.
3) Concurrency validation: we'll run synthetic clients that emulate bursts (300 concurrent clients ramping to 600 over 2 minutes). Confirm Redwood can simulate the same routing to a dedicated pool for those tests.

Procurement: procurement@nebulahealth.com is the right address. I copied ops+prod for scheduling. We'll plan to confirm the exact canary windows internally and come back within two business days.

Also — are you able to provide a short example of the per-request log format ahead of the test so our SREs can validate ingestion?

Appreciate it,
Aaron
Director, Platform Engineering
NebulaHealth
aaron.li@nebulahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron.li@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, ops+prod@nebulahealth.com <ops+prod@nebulahealth.com>, procurement@nebulahealth.com <procurement@nebulahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO acceptance testing checklist & reporting playbook

Aaron — thanks for the quick read. Short answers inline below, then an updated action list.

> Can Redwood extract chunk timestamps in the artifact?
Yes — we'll include per-chunk timestamps in the raw logs and a prebuilt script that emits the inter-arrival histogram. The raw log format we'll provide is a single CSV with one line per chunk: request_id, chunk_index, chunk_timestamp_utc, bytes, model_variant, host_id. Example attached in reporting-playbook-v1.xlsx (sheet: artifacts).

> Cold-start handling definition
We can support the "first request to a model instance within 60s of no traffic" definition. Implementation note: that requires us to surface a flag in the logs so the canary analysis can exclude those samples. We'll include that in the artifact under the column "is_cold_start".

> Concurrency validation / routing to dedicated pool
Confirm — for the canary window Redwood can pin your test traffic to a dedicated capacity pool (reserved) so the routing path matches production reserved behavior. We'll provide the test API key and endpoint that routes to that pool.

Artifacts & reporting cadence (proposed):
- Raw logs: per-request and per-chunk CSV delivered within 24 hours of each test window.
- Aggregates: daily CSV with p50/p95/p99, mean throughput, concurrency histogram.
- Weekly summary: one-page incident log + preliminary scores.
- Monthly: SLA PDF with credits table and month-to-date performance.

Exclusions (finalized):
- Customer network / CDN issues not originated within Redwood network.
- Scheduled maintenance with >72 hour advance notice.
- Cold-starts as defined above (first request within 60s to an idle container).

Remedies (short):
- Tiered credits: 5% monthly credit for single SLO miss, 10% for two separate misses in a month, escalation to engineering review + remediation plan after third miss. Legal can tighten language in the contract.

Proposed test windows: Oct 5, Oct 6, Oct 7 — 0800–1200 PT. Please confirm which day(s) you want Redwood to run the synthetic load and whether you want streaming and non-streaming profiles on the same window.

I've attached the reporting-playbook-v1.xlsx with: sample CSV rows, artifact layout, and a draft checklist for the canary run. Also re-attached the measurement PDF for convenience.

If this looks good I'll ask Ben/Legal to begin drafting the short SLA clause and remedies table for your procurement team.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128
